purpose: Research-only evidence packet for five individually registered Dublin City NIAH structures

source_snapshot.queue_rule: Each selected registration number was checked as an exact entry in the workflow-generated Dublin missing-registration queue.

official_dataset_reference.title: NIAH Data Download
official_dataset_reference.note: Official national CSV provides ITM coordinates and latitude/longitude. Individual NIAH page coordinate pairs are preserved separately as raw values because the page does not label their CRS.

candidate_records.name: North Star Hotel
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010124 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced ten-bay, three-storey, double-pile Victorian stucco-faced hotel, built c.1880. NIAH notes its difficult triangular site between the overhead Loop-line railway and Amiens Street, and its role in servicing the developing railway system. Its architectural treatment includes stucco architraves and decorative panels, a principal round-arched entrance and a calp-stone gable wall adjoining the railway structure.

candidate_records.name: Dublin City Coroner's Court
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010127 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Terraced building built in 1901, comprising a two-storey, two-bay block with a projecting double-height gable-fronted end bay to the east. NIAH describes red-brick Flemish-bond walls, sandstone detailing and carved CORONER'S COURT lettering. The official register records original and current use as courthouse. The missing-registration queue has no separate appraisal text for this entry; no additional appraisal claims are inferred.

candidate_records.name: The Harbourmaster (former Dock Offices)
candidate_records.address: George's Dock / Harbourmaster Place, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010128 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Detached three-bay, two-storey brick former harbourmaster's house or Dock Offices, built c.1830, with a three-stage tower and clock faces. NIAH records its later conversion to a pub and restaurant and its relationship to the lock-side setting between George's Dock and Inner Dock. It is a separate registered building, distinct from the lock and winches nearby.

candidate_records.name: George's Dock — pair of dock winches
candidate_records.address: East side of the lock, George's Dock / Custom House Harbour, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010129 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Pair of cast- and wrought-iron winches erected c.1830 on the east side of the lock linking Inner Dock with George's Dock. The NIAH describes cog-wheels, axles and crank handles mounted on iron brackets fixed to a granite base. The appraisal explains that the winches were used to pull ships closer to dock walls. Treat the pair as the single NIAH-registered object; do not split each winch into an independent registration.

candidate_records.name: George's Dock — limestone lock
candidate_records.address: George's Dock / Custom House Harbour, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010130 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Limestone lock built c.1825 connecting George's Dock to Inner Dock. NIAH describes paired squared and coursed limestone ashlar walls, granite coping, curved ends where former lock gates were located, and later alterations including a modern steel bridge. The appraisal says the lock is no longer in use and has been retained in the docklands redevelopment. This is a separate registered structure from the winches (50010129) and former Dock Offices (50010128).

spatial_and_identity_cautions: 50010124 is the North Star Hotel on a difficult triangular site adjacent to the Loop-line railway. Do not conflate it with the railway bridge or other railway structures.
50010127 is the separate Coroner's Court building on Store Street.
50010128 is the former Dock Offices/Harbourmaster's house.
50010129 is a pair of dock winches recorded as one registered object. Do not split the pair into separate records.
50010130 is the limestone lock connecting George's Dock and Inner Dock. It is separate from the winches and former Dock Offices.
The three George's Dock registrations form a related maritime/industrial group but retain separate identities and source references.
Individual NIAH page coordinate pairs are preserved as raw values because the page does not label their CRS. Do not interpret them as EPSG:2157 or overwrite official CSV coordinates.
NIAH descriptions of use, condition and alterations are survey-time source statements, not present-day field verification.
No physical access, ownership, public access or current condition has been verified.
explicitly_not_done: No visual inventory or source registry imports
No map pins or coordinate imports
